standard_prerequisites.name: The hypercohomology spectral sequence arises from the filtered-object construction applied to the canonical truncation filtration of K
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces convergence to vanishing and agreement statements for the truncations.

standard_prerequisites.name: On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme the cohomology of a suitable truncation vanishes in large degree of the filtration index, by the nice-K-injective application with the global sections functor and the quasi-coherence bound on higher direct images
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the first requirement H^n(X, tau_leq_-p K) = 0 for p >> 0.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a general ringed space, the canonical truncation does not change H^n once -p <= n
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the second requirement for p << 0.

core_obligations: Reduction: recall the construction of the spectral sequence by the cohomology filtered-object lemma with filtration tau_leq_-p K; convergence reduces to H^n(X, tau_leq_-p K) = 0 for p >> 0 and H^n(X, K) = H^n(X, tau_leq_-p K) for p << 0 (proof lines 782-792).

First requirement: apply the nice-K-injective vanishing lemma with F = Gamma(X, -) together with the bound on higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules on quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes (proof lines 793-796).
Second requirement: for -p <= n the canonical truncation tau_leq_-p K agrees with K in degree n on any ringed space, so the cohomology groups agree (proof lines 797-799).
Conclude the spectral sequence is bounded and converges (statement).
proof_roadmap: Reduce convergence of the filtered-object spectral sequence to two statements about canonical truncations (proof lines 782-792).
Prove vanishing for p >> 0 by the nice-K-injective application and the higher-direct-image bound (proof lines 793-796).
Prove agreement for p << 0 by the degree-wise triviality of the truncation (proof lines 797-799).
